status_summary: The SEC issued a final rule, published 2025-03-14 at 90 FR 12105 and effective that day, that removes the delegation to the Director of the Division of Enforcement to issue formal orders of investigation, the orders that designate staff who may issue subpoenas; the Commission said the change aligns investigative resources with Commission priorities. This returns to the Commission the decision to open formal investigations, the main delegated step at the start of an enforcement case. A separate final rule published 2026-07-20 (91 FR 45187, effective 2026-07-26) moves registration-related delegations to the EDGAR Business Office and does not change Enforcement delegations or describe any study of narrowing or sunsetting delegations, and no such study was found.

timeline.event: The SEC published a final rule (90 FR 12105, effective the same day) removing the Division of Enforcement Director's authority to issue formal orders of investigation.
The SEC published a final rule on modernizing delegations to staff (91 FR 45187, effective 2026-07-26) that shifts registration-related delegations and leaves enforcement delegations unchanged.

title: End staff delegation of the decision to open SEC enforcement cases; study delegations
uncertainties: The 2025-03-14 rule (90 FR 12105) was re-read in this review on federalregister.gov through a summarizing fetch tool; it removes and reserves 17 CFR 200.30-4(a)(13) (Release Nos. 33-11366, 34-102552, IA-6862, IC-35492) and recalls that the 2009 delegation was first made for one year to allow Commission review before being extended in 2010, which is history rather than a new study. The 2026-07-20 rule (91 FR 45187) was read in full by the researcher. The rule does not say whether the decision to file an enforcement action was ever delegated; that filing an action requires a Commission vote is from general knowledge, so the formal-order delegation is treated as the delegated decision the Mandate targets, a judgment call. No internal delegation review or GAO study of SEC delegations was found on sec.gov or federalregister.gov; the absence is not proof none exists.
